key_insight: The paper shows that simple domain generalization can make pixel-level tampering detectors robust across different modern VLMs, despite major shifts in how edits are generated. In short: train for cross-model diversity, and localization becomes much more reliable on unseen manipulations.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of detecting and localizing image tampering when the manipulated images come from different VLMs and unseen distributions. Existing detectors often fail to generalize across models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Qwen-Image.
method: Study domain generalization specifically for pixel-level tampering localization in modern VLM-generated images.
Learn a detector that captures manipulation patterns shared across different VLMs rather than overfitting to one generation model.
Evaluate robustness under cross-model and out-of-distribution shifts to ensure the detector works on unseen tampering sources.
impact: This matters for practitioners building forensic tools, content moderation systems, and trust/safety pipelines because VLM-generated edits are rapidly evolving. A detector that generalizes across models is more practical for real-world deployment than one tuned to a single generator.

paper_title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs
paper_authors: Yi Tang, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Cui, Sondos Mahmoud Bsharat, Jiacheng Liu
